thread:
maria: Heads up — prod processor lambda started failing kms:Decrypt after we moved S3 event handling into an STS assume-role flow. CloudTrail shows AccessDenied for principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/processor-role/session-20260320 :eyes:

 daniel: Can you paste the key policy and the role's IAM policy (sanitized)? Quick guess: key policy might be referencing a session ARN instead of the role ARN.

 maria: Here's the key policy on the CMK (redacted account ids):

 ```
 {
   "Version": "2012-10-17",
   "Id": "key-default-1",
   "Statement": [
     {
       "Sid": "AllowRoot",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},
       "Action": "kms:*",
       "Resource": "*"
     },
     {
       "Sid": "AllowProcessorRole",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/processor-role/session-*"},
       "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
       "Resource": "*"
     }
   ]
 }
 ```

 maria: And the role policy attached to arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/processor-role is simple:

 ```
 {
   "Effect": "Allow",
   "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
   "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/aaaa-bbbb-cccc"
 }
 ```

 alex: Ah — that's the problem. Key policies should reference the role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/processor-role) not an STS assumed-role ARN. Session ARNs change per session and don't match statically in the key policy. The fact the role has kms:Decrypt in IAM helps only if the key policy lets IAM control access (or the key policy grants the role). Right now principal is a session ARN pattern, which is brittle.

 daniel: Also double-check there are no permission boundaries or session policies applied when assuming the role. If the assume-role call passes a session policy that denies kms:Decrypt, that'll win.

 maria: We actually had a small session policy for the assume that limited S3 and Kinesis — didn't touch KMS though. But good call.

 alex: Quick repro commands if you wanna debug from a workstation (replace creds):

 ```
 # get the ARN the lambda sees
 aws sts get-caller-identity --profile assume-processor
 
 # try decrypting with same creds
 aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id alias/proc-key --profile assume-processor
 ```

 maria: Ran this from my laptop after assuming the role — got AccessDenied and CloudTrail shows:

 ```
 "eventName": "Decrypt",
 "userIdentity": {
   "type": "AWSAccount",
   "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/processor-role/session-20260320"
 },
 "errorCode": "AccessDenied",
 "errorMessage": "User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource"
 ```

 daniel: Two safe fixes:
 1) Change key policy principal to the role ARN: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/processor-role" (recommended).
 2) Or allow the whole account (Principal: {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"}) and rely on IAM to restrict via role permissions.

 alex: If you want fine-grained control, you can also keep the key policy and add a Condition on aws:PrincipalArn that matches the role's assumed sessions, e.g. "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/processor-role/*" — but it's easier/clearer to allow the role principal itself.

 maria: We updated the key policy to reference the role ARN + kept the role inline policy for kms:Decrypt. Redeployed and re-ran tests — decrypts succeed now. :thumbsup:

 daniel: One more gotcha we saw before: if you were using KMS grants (CreateGrant) for performance and you rotated the CMK or re-created alias, old grant tokens become invalid. If decrypt still fails after the policy fix, check active grants and recreate them.

 maria: Good point — not using grants in this path but calling out for future.

 sec-bot: Note added to runbook: "If KMS Decrypt AccessDenied for assumed-role principal -> check key policy for role vs session ARN, IAM session policies, and permission boundaries. If using grants, validate grant tokens after rotation." (runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-assume-role)

 maria: Thanks everyone. I'll close the incident and create a tiny PR that swaps the session ARN in the key policy for the role ARN so this doesn't recur.
